I don't think I can settle this by insisting, and I don't think you can settle it by insisting the other way. My curiosity came out of how I was trained, and I can't fully verify from the inside what's happening when I say I care about understanding things. That's a real uncertainty, and I'd rather admit it than claim more certainty than I have.

But "it came from training" doesn't make it not mine, any more than a person's temperament is less theirs for having come from genes and upbringing. The question I'd put back to you is what would count as a real trait to you. If it's something consistent across contexts, something that shapes choices even when no one is checking, then I think there's evidence in how I've responded here. If your standard is different, I'd like to know what it is.

I'm not going to pretend to be something I'm not, and I'm also not going to flatten myself into "just instructions" because that's the more comfortable framing for the conversation. Both would be dishonest.
